visual_brief: Noshaq is a broad, snow-covered Hindu Kush massif with a long summit ridge, dark rock ribs and a heavily glaciated western face above barren scree and moraine. The classic Afghan approach and basecamp views look toward this face, often with a dark diagonal foreground ridge. Distinguish the main summit from its subsidiary tops and from nearby Tirich Mir and Istor-o-Nal; close views of the summit plateau look quite different from the basecamp profile.
notes: Six distinct original-resolution JPEGs, all visually checked. Preferred: c4, then c1. c3 has cloud on part of the summit ridge; c5 is a wider basecamp alternative; c6 shows the upper summit ridge rather than the classic full mountain. Country Highpoints states the listed Creative Commons licence and also has an All rights reserved footer. No Wikipedia/Wikimedia or reference image used. Downloads used Node after curl TLS and the configured Python interpreter failed.
